speaker: Patient
text: 16-year-old female. The patient has not experienced menarche. She was noted to have partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly at birth. The patient's mother reports that during pregnancy she had abnormal hair growth on her chin. The patient has a history of severe acne and has sustained fractures following minor trauma. text: The significantly elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone and virilization strongly point to 21-hydroxylase deficiency. speaker: Doctor
text: With normal electrolytes and renin, this confirms simple virilizing congenital adrenal hyperplasia rather than the salt-wasting form. The bone fragility is likely due to chronic glucocorticoid excess or previous undertreatment suppressing gonadal function. Do you have any history of early pubic hair development or rapid growth in childhood?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Delayed menarche. I also have Severe acne, History of fractures following minor trauma, Partial labial fusion and clitoromegaly noted at birth.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of ambiguous genitalia at birth, elevated 17-hydroxyprogesterone, and normal electrolytes confirms a diagnosis of simple virilizing congenital adrenal hyperplasia. The bone fragility is likely secondary to chronic androgen excess and suppressed estrogen levels due to the lack of menarche. DIAGNOSIS READY: Simple virilizing congenital adrenal hyperplasia (21-hydroxylase deficiency)
